# Summary of Cairn Rules

## Pulses
A pulse makes a cairn taller by adding two components: a fixed stride amount plus a bonus based on current height. The bonus equals how many complete stride-lengths fit into the current height (using integer division). When applying multiple pulses in sequence, you must recalculate the stride count fresh each time, since the height changes after each pulse.

## Leaks
A leak removes marks after a pulse occurs. The number of marks lost equals how many complete leak-units fit into the new (post-pulse) height. Leaks are height-dependent — taller cairns lose more marks.

## Drains
Unlike leaks, drains remove a fixed number of marks every cycle, regardless of height. A cycle consists of one pulse followed by the drain removal. The cairn eventually reaches zero when the drain's fixed removal outpaces what pulses can add.

## Working Backwards
To find an original height before pulses occurred, reverse the pulse logic: ask what height would produce the final result. This requires reasoning through the pulse formula rather than using arithmetic shortcuts, since the amount added depends on the starting height.

## Merging Cairns
Two cairns combine into one using weighted shares (expressed as decimals) and a tether value. Each cairn contributes a fractional part of its height (floored), then the tether adjusts the final result. The tether is essential — shares alone don't determine the merged height.
